entries.test: International governance implementation records, US agency mandates, and documented federal cybercrime capabilities as of May 16, 2025 would establish whether these governance structures and capabilities existed or had deteriorated.
entries.note: The cybercrime assessment is imprecise but has a plain reading about operational preparedness.

entries.test: Public reporting and fraud statistics available by May 16, 2025, together with federal enforcement and coordination records, would establish whether many accounts documented a sharp increase in AI-fueled scams and whether a coordinated federal response existed.
entries.note: “By many accounts” qualifies the reported increase and is preserved in the proposition.

entries.test: Republican statements, legislative proposals, votes, and administration policies in 2023 versus those by May 16, 2025 would show whether opposition to AI regulation increased substantially and pro-regulation Republicans lost influence over policy.
entries.note: “Drowned out” has a plain contextual reading about political influence; “seemed sincerely interested” describes an impression.

entries.test: Altman's public Senate testimony in May 2023 and May 2025 would show whether his positions shifted from supporting AI regulation to consistently opposing regulatory proposals.
entries.note: In context, “no longer talking about AI regulation” means no longer advocating it.
“Phenomenal” is a subjective appraisal of Altman's social skill. The sincerity qualification also concerns his private state of mind.
The surrounding text clearly implies that Altman cannot be trusted. That overall judgment has no agreed factual threshold.
